content.purpose: Read any command, however unfamiliar, and say which part is which.
content.mentalModel: Every command line is the same shape: command [options] [arguments]. The command is the program to run. Options change how it behaves and conventionally start with a dash. Arguments are what it acts on. The shell splits the line on spaces, which is why a filename containing a space becomes two arguments unless you quote it, and why an accidental space can change what a command does entirely.

demonstration.explanation: ls is the command, -l is an option asking for the long format, and /home/student is the argument saying which directory to list.
echo received three separate arguments, not one. The shell split them on the spaces before echo ever saw them.

remember: The shell splits the line on spaces before the command runs
Options usually start with a dash; arguments usually do not
dangerous: An unintended space turns one argument into two, which is how rm -rf /home /student happens

tasks.instruction: List your home directory in the long format and save the result to /home/student/long-listing.txt. Use one command with one option and one argument.

validators.message: long-listing.txt does not look like a long listing. The long format starts each line with permission characters.

hints: The command that lists directory contents is ls.
The option asking for the long format is -l.

tasks.instruction: Someone meant to print one sentence but got three words on separate arguments. Work out why, then create a file called split-explained.txt containing the word spaces.
tasks.diagnosis: echo received three arguments, because the shell collapsed the runs of spaces while splitting the line. echo then printed its arguments separated by a single space each, so the extra spacing disappeared. Quoting the text as "Hello   world    again" would have made it a single argument and preserved the spacing exactly.
hints: What does the shell do to the line before echo runs?

reviewQuestions.question: In cp -r website website-backup, which part is an option?
reviewQuestions.explanation: cp is the command; website and website-backup are arguments; -r is the option that makes it recurse.
